messages:
sasha: quick follow-up to the islandization RFC — sketched an implementation sketch for tenant 'islands' + a background compactor. main goal: reduce cross-tenant fragmentation and make per-tenant eviction predictable.

ajay: can you TL;DR the differences vs current slab/arena approach?

sasha: today we have shared slab pools with soft quotas. fragmentation happens when many tenants allocate weird sizes and we end up with tiny unusable gaps. islandization = give each tenant a configurable set of contiguous arenas (e.g. 256MiB chunks) and prefer colocating short-lived allocations into a tenant-local bump allocator.

maria: so this is basically per-tenant arenas + occasional global reclaim? what's the compactor doing?

sasha: compactor runs in background, epochally picks candidate arenas that are <X% live, migrates live allocations into a new arena using async cudaMemcpy/peer-copy where possible, then frees the old arena. migration is tenant-local so we can avoid cross-tenant pinning.

kai: how do we handle latency-sensitive inference requests that touch an allocation during compaction? stalls?

sasha: plan: transparent transient forwarding. when compactor starts copying an object it leaves a forward pointer in the old slot. read path checks a cheap bit; if forwarded, it follows pointer. fast-path stays in L1 otherwise. we already have a fast atomic load to check residency bit in runtime.

ajay: forwarding adds indirection cost — measurable on 8k token streams. do we have fallbacks?

sasha: we only forward for objects below threshold (small tensors). big KV cache rows are migrated only during idle windows. also compactor throttles based on tail-latency SLOs (observability hooks).

oliver: what about NUMA + host staging? moving pages between GPUs and host pinned memory is heavy. are we planning host-side compaction too?

sasha: yes — two-layer compaction. GPU-to-GPU via peer copy when same node; cross-node we prefer reallocation in resident host staging and then async RDMA if available. host-side compaction reclaims fragmentation in host-staging pools, evict pressure is signalled via the same epoch controller.

maria: curious about fairness — could a noisy tenant force compactions and thrash others?

sasha: islands are rate-limited by tenant compaction budget. noisy tenant gets throttled; we expose per-tenant compaction and migration meters in console. operator can increase budget for enterprise Dedicated tenants if they accept cost.

kai: any safety concerns with pointer forwarding and GC? race conditions?

sasha: we use atomic CAS state transitions: FREE -> COPYING -> FORWARDING -> FREED. reader path checks state and either reads in-place or follows forward pointer. compactor finalizes with a tombstone and free. tests in the prototype catch ABA by versioning pointers.

ajay: can we get a config example?

sasha: pasted small snippet below:

```
compaction:
  enabled: true
  tenant_islands: true
  default_arena_size: 268435456 # 256MiB
  copying_budget_ms_per_epoch: 200
  small_tensor_threshold_bytes: 65536
  tail_latency_guard_ms: 10
```

maria: nice. can we run this on a small fleet ring to validate perf before wider rollout?

sasha: yes propose A/B: 10% nodes with islands=on, collect hotset churn, token latency p95, and migration bytes. devops-bot: scheduled canary rollout for eng-runtime ring-3 tonight at 02:00 UTC — will post metrics when done.

devops-bot: canary deploy started: islands=true on 3 nodes (ring-3). monitor: /metrics/islandization/*

oliver: next steps — get bench numbers for long-running busy tenants (embedding pipelines) and chat workloads. also need security review for pointer metadata in host memory.

sasha: thanks all — I'll push the compactor prototype branch and a perf test harness. will ping when ready for review. :rocket:
